question: Can a duplicate adapter edge with a changed outer intent token and unchanged nested adapter token split into another identity group while the original pair remains complete?
hypothesis: An adapter row whose outer identity disagrees with nested adapter-edge identity must invalidate both identity groups implicated by the contradiction, so the original receipt cannot retain exposed timing.
treatment: Freeze #7690 head and retained A01 fixture. Mutate one duplicate DOWN and one duplicate UP by changing only the outer intent_token, leaving nested adapter_edge identity unchanged. Run existing exact/unknown/legacy regressions plus these two outer-vs-nested token mutations against the frozen baseline and candidate projector.
decision_rule: Baseline expected to leave original pairs complete for both copied rows. Candidate must pass all four exact test methods; both conflict cases must return no paired adapter receipt and null intervals for every adapter receipt. Existing five duplicate, four unknown-event and two legacy-transition cases remain closed.
controls: Exact unique retained DOWN/UP; five prior exact/conflicting duplicates; unknown event discriminator cases; supported legacy transition outer-name cases.
uncertainty: One synthetic retained X-adapter fixture and deterministic projector only; no live X-server, physical dwell, application consumption, task effect, threat response, recovery or MAP01 result.
